text: Root cause analysis still means reproduce, isolate, and confirm. What an LLM adds is speed on the first step: reading a wall of logs and proposing where to look.
A useful draft needs the exact error and stack trace, the log lines before the failure, which stage failed, and what changed recently.
An LLM's draft reads persuasively — but that confidence isn't evidence. It's pattern-matching your error against similar failures it has seen before.
The draft earns its keep on repetitive failures, confirming a human's instinct in seconds. It's worth far less on a genuinely novel failure with no pattern to match.
A fast first hypothesis, always confirmed before it's trusted. Next up: AI-assisted schema mapping.
